name: Onboard new customers with Jira and Microsoft Teams with instant alerts

nodes.name: Receive Inbound Webhook
nodes.notes: Entry point: listens for POST calls on /wf08623-task. Use the TEST url while building, switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after publishing. Watch out: While building use the TEST url; switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after you publish.

nodes.name: Prepare Approval Packet
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes requestId, summary, requestedBy. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Request Approval via Microsoft Teams
nodes.notes: Posts a chat message into a Microsoft Teams channel — same role as a Slack notify, for teams standardized on Teams. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Microsoft OAuth2. Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.

nodes.name: Hold for Decision
nodes.notes: Pauses the execution until the resume webhook is called — this is the approval/HITL gate. Watch out: Long waits survive restarts, but the resume URL is single-use.

nodes.name: Approved?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.body?.decision || $json.decision }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Apply Approved Change (Google Sheets)
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Task Tracker', matched on taskId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Record Decline + Notify Requester
nodes.notes: Posts a chat message into a Microsoft Teams channel — same role as a Slack notify, for teams standardized on Teams. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Microsoft OAuth2. Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.

nodes.name: Join Decision Paths
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Guard Non-Empty title
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

# Onboard new customers for standups

**Pattern:** Onboarding Sequence · **Level:** Beginner · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers standups work end to end across Microsoft Teams and Google Sheets.

It moves through 9 working steps, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Prepare Approval Packet
3. Request Approval via Microsoft Teams
4. Hold for Decision
5. Approved?
6. Apply Approved Change (Google Sheets)
7. Record Decline + Notify Requester
8. Join Decision Paths
9. Guard Non-Empty title

## Why it exists

Doing standups work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Prepare Approval Packet → Request Approval via Microsoft Teams → Hold for Decision → Approved? → Apply Approved Change (Google Sheets) → Record Decline + Notify Requester → Join Decision Paths → Guard Non-Empty title

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Microsoft Teams and Google Sheets aligned by hand for standups
- Standups sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Microsoft Teams
- Pushing standups events into Microsoft Teams and Google Sheets the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Standups work where "Prepare Approval Packet" is still a manual step before Microsoft Teams

## You get

- Keeps Microsoft Teams and Google Sheets in step for standups, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Microsoft Teams or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 9 nodes in this standups build
- Branches rejoin before Microsoft Teams, so a standups run reports once rather than 9 times
- The pause before Microsoft Teams is durable — a standups run survives a restart
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 9 nodes for standups before wiring Microsoft Teams

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The workflow pauses on a Wait node configured to resume via webhook — n8n's actual human-in-the-loop primitive, not a polling loop. The resume URL is embedded directly in the approval message so approving is one click, and the paused execution burns no compute for however long the decision takes.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Add a timeout to the Wait node so unanswered approvals auto-decline after N hours.
2. Change the approval channel and confirm the resume link still works.
3. Add a third outcome (e.g. 'needs changes') alongside approve/decline.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Microsoft Teams: restrict the app registration to the target team; tenant-wide permission is not needed to post.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole standups payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🙋 Human in the loop

The workflow pauses at the Wait node until a human posts a decision to the resume URL (included in the approval message). Approve → the action executes; anything else → recorded as declined. No timeout is set by default — add one under the Wait node's options if approvals go stale.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your standups process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
